A.notes: Packet issue: A's screenshots (both 1440 and 390) contain Cadence SaaS-page content in the top ~two-thirds, with only the photography/tone/applications sections of Halcyon visible; sections 01-04 (logo, palette, type) were not visible in the render, though the source has h2s for them. Source has no logo usage rules (no do/don't, clearspace), so the brief's 'logo with usage rules' is not met. Audit: contrast fails (white caption on image 1.17:1, 3.35:1 eyebrow, 3.9:1 on terracotta), tiny text 6.5-9px in illustrations, no prefers-reduced-motion rule. Visible Halcyon parts: warm azelejo-blue/terracotta/cream palette is charming and the packaging/cup/shopfront illustrations are tidy, voice before/after is good, but overall it is a competent template with 4 saturated hues.

B.notes: Strong concept: the roast-curve device (interactive scrubbable profile) threads through mark, bags, cup and signage. Complete brand guide: logo with clearspace, min sizes, colourways, six misuse examples, computed contrast pair table with a 'not for text' case, roast ladder, type scale with tracking/leading, numerals/localisation, photography direction, say/not tone rules with tabs, applications, versioning. Instrument Serif/Hanken/JetBrains Mono used with intent. Audit gates all pass, but at 390 the hero's giant ember disc sits behind the intro paragraph and tags, making that text illegible (fails G1/G2 by eye); mobile nav is a clipped horizontal scroller; photography is abstract placeholders; 1 small touch-target warning.

why: B delivers every requested section with real depth and a distinctive, functional signature idea, while A (as rendered, with Cadence content contaminating its screenshots) omits logo usage rules and fails contrast and minimum-text gates. B's mobile hero overlap needs fixing before launch, but it is far closer to shippable.
